physical_state_in: Natural surface water or groundwater at source
D_parameters: legal abstraction limits (WFD permits); minimum ecological flow requirements; intake capacity
C_parameters: surface water (65%) and groundwater (35%) sources; municipal industrial and agricultural use types
notes: Municipal abstraction ~8.5 km3/yr across basin. EU member states require WFD Article 11 abstraction permits. AQUASTAT reports annual abstraction by country and sector. Non-EU members have variable permit frameworks. Opacity score: 1.

physical_state_out: Raw water delivered to treatment works
D_parameters: pipeline capacity limits; pumping head requirements; conveyance loss targets
C_parameters: raw water delivered to multiple treatment works serving different population centres
notes: Conveyance losses typically 2-5%. Energy intensity ~0.12 kWh/m3. Large utilities (Vienna; Budapest; Bucharest) operate extensive raw water aqueducts up to 80km. Data available via national utility reports and Eurostat energy in water sector statistics. Opacity score: 1.

measurable_output: Treated water volume meeting drinking water standards
D_parameters: strict WHO/EU water quality standards (>100 parameters); treatment process specifications; chemical dosing protocols; quality monitoring requirements
C_parameters: drinking water delivered to distribution system; reuse water for industrial supply (some utilities)
notes: EU Drinking Water Directive compliance >99.5% for EU members. Treatment energy intensity ~0.35 kWh/m3 — most energy-intensive phase. Emerging contaminants (pharmaceuticals; microplastics) represent next regulatory frontier. WHO/UNICEF JMP tracks access and safety. Opacity score: 1.

physical_state_in: Treated water at treatment works outlet
physical_state_out: Treated water in consumer distribution mains
primary_transformation: Pressure management; pumping; service reservoir storage
D_parameters: pressure zone boundaries; pipe age and condition (avg 35 years); leakage detection capability; service reservoir capacity
C_parameters: water delivered to all consumer types: residential; commercial; industrial; fire fighting; public
notes: Non-revenue water ~25% average across basin (12% in Austria/Germany; 40% in parts of Romania/Moldova/Ukraine). Network condition is key D parameter. IBNET benchmarks available. Detailed network topology is commercially sensitive — key opacity in this phase. Pipe material includes asbestos cement in older networks. Opacity score: 2.

D_parameters: meter accuracy standards; connection regulations; pressure at consumer point
C_parameters: ~88% of 81 million basin population (~71 million served); 160 litres/person/day average
notes: ~88% access to safely managed drinking water (JMP 2023). Unserved ~9.7 million concentrated in rural areas: Romania; Ukraine; Moldova; Bosnia. Consumption data available via JMP and Eurostat. Metering coverage >95% in EU members; lower in non-EU countries. Opacity score: 1.
